tls_enabled.title: TLS/SSL Enabled on Database Connection
tls_enabled.description: Whether the application's database connection is configured to use TLS/SSL encryption for transport

certificate_verification_mode.title: Server Certificate Verification Mode
certificate_verification_mode.description: The level of server certificate validation enforced when establishing the TLS connection to the database. Controls whether CA chain and hostname are verified.

db_network_exposure.title: Database Network Exposure Level
db_network_exposure.description: The network segment or exposure level of the application-to-database communication path

minimum_tls_version.title: Minimum TLS Version
minimum_tls_version.description: The minimum TLS protocol version negotiated or accepted for database connections

weak_cipher_suites_enabled.title: Weak or Deprecated Cipher Suites Enabled
weak_cipher_suites_enabled.description: Whether any weak, deprecated, or export-grade cipher suites are permitted on the database connection (RC4, 3DES, NULL, EXPORT, DES)

tls_enforced_on_connection.title: TLS Enforced on Database Connection
tls_enforced_on_connection.description: Whether TLS/SSL is required (not merely optional) for all application-to-database connections, with no plaintext fallback permitted

ssl_mode.title: SSL/TLS Mode
ssl_mode.description: The SSL/TLS enforcement mode configured on the database connection (client or server side), controlling whether encryption is required, preferred, or disabled, and whether certificates are verified.

certificate_authority_validation_enforce.title: Certificate Authority Validation Enforced
certificate_authority_validation_enforce.description: Whether the application driver is explicitly configured to validate the database server's certificate against a trusted CA chain, rejecting connections to servers with self-signed or untrusted certificates.

hostname_verification_enabled.title: Hostname Verification Enabled
hostname_verification_enabled.description: Whether the application driver verifies that the certificate's CN or SAN matches the database server hostname, preventing impersonation via a certificate issued to a different host.

plaintext_fallback_permitted.title: Plaintext Fallback Permitted
plaintext_fallback_permitted.description: Whether the server or client configuration explicitly allows falling back to an unencrypted connection if TLS negotiation fails or is not offered by the peer.

app_layer_query_signing_enabled.title: Application-Layer Query Signing/MAC Enabled
app_layer_query_signing_enabled.description: Whether the application applies a cryptographic signature or MAC to SQL queries before transmission, independent of TLS

tls_termination_point.title: TLS Termination Point
tls_termination_point.description: Where TLS is terminated before reaching the database — at the application itself, at an intermediate proxy/pooler, or at a load balancer

internal_segment_encryption_enforced.title: Internal Segment Encryption Enforced Post-Proxy
internal_segment_encryption_enforced.description: Whether a separate TLS or encrypted tunnel is enforced on the internal network segment between the proxy/pooler and the database server

connection_rate_limiting_enabled.title: Connection Rate Limiting Enabled
connection_rate_limiting_enabled.description: Whether the application-to-database data flow enforces a maximum connection request rate, preventing flood attacks or runaway process scenarios.

query_throttling_enabled.title: Query Throttling Enabled
query_throttling_enabled.description: Whether the application-to-database channel enforces limits on query volume or query rate (queries per second) to prevent denial-of-service via query flooding.

max_connections_per_client_configured.title: Max Connections Per Client Configured
max_connections_per_client_configured.description: Whether a maximum number of simultaneous connections from the application client to the database is explicitly configured, capping resource exhaustion from a single compromised or misbehaving client.

pooler_to_db_tls_enabled.title: Pooler-to-Database TLS Enabled
pooler_to_db_tls_enabled.description: Whether TLS encryption is enforced on the connection from the connection pooler (PgBouncer, ProxySQL, RDS Proxy) to the backend database server.

pooler_server_tls_certificate_validation.title: Pooler Server-Side TLS Certificate Validation Mode
pooler_server_tls_certificate_validation.description: The certificate validation mode used by the pooler when connecting to the database, controlling whether the pooler verifies the database server's TLS certificate to prevent MITM attacks.

internal_network_segment_access_control.title: Internal Network Segment Access Control
internal_network_segment_access_control.description: The level of network access control enforced on the internal segment between the connection pooler and the database (e.g., firewall rules, security groups, micro-segmentation).

multi_datacenter_or_cloud_peered.title: Multi-Datacenter or Cloud-Peered Deployment
multi_datacenter_or_cloud_peered.description: Indicates whether the deployment spans multiple datacenters or uses cloud network peering, creating exposure to dynamic routing infrastructure such as BGP.

tls_certificate_validation_enforced.title: TLS Certificate Validation Enforced
tls_certificate_validation_enforced.description: Whether strict TLS certificate validation (including hostname verification and CA chain validation) is enforced on application-to-database connections, preventing interception via rogue certificates introduced through route hijacking.

bgp_route_filtering_configured.title: BGP Route Filtering Configured
bgp_route_filtering_configured.description: Whether BGP prefix filters, route policies, or RPKI-based origin validation are configured on peering sessions that carry application-to-database traffic, preventing unauthorized route injection.
